solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quiet house facing endless prejudice and fear

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly

indicators.note: endless tells us to drop the final letter of the word for prejudice

parts.note: bias means prejudice

explanation.surface: A silent household is gripped by bigotry and fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an irrational, intense fear of something, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: A right problematical situation when there's nothing in wardrobe

indicators.note: in tells us the zero goes inside the word for a mess

parts.note: to be in the mire is to be in a difficult situation
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone finds a real problem when the wardrobe turns out to be empty.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a large ornate cupboard or wardrobe, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: 'Stupid boy' will be brought before teachers, that's very plain

indicators.note: will be brought before tells us the boy's name sits in front of the teachers' word

parts.note: Pike is the young private Captain Mainwaring calls 'stupid boy' in the British TV sitcom Dad's Army
a school's teachers are its staff

explanation.surface: A dim lad is hauled up in front of the staff, which is perfectly obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard; Private Pike is its hapless youngest member.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff' means utterly obvious, so the word alone stands for very plain.

clue.text: Drink disgusting pop in Syrian city

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

indicators.note: disgusting suggests something spoiled or messed up, signalling these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sips revolting fizzy pop while in a Syrian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major city in northern Syria, one of the oldest continuously inhabited places.

clue.text: Reproach worker maybe when protecting scoundrel

indicators.note: protecting means the insect's letters wrap round and shield the rogue

parts.note: a worker is a kind of bee, hence the maybe
a rat is a scoundrel or traitor

explanation.surface: Someone scolds an employee for shielding a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate someone is to scold or reproach them angrily, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: She's not fair catch, nabbed by cruel person

indicators.note: nabbed by means the catching word is seized and held inside the cruel person

parts.note: a brute is a cruel, savage person
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: A woman who is no fair prize gets grabbed by a heartless man.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark hair, so she is not fair-haired.

clue.text: Bishop spanning many years becomes angry person

indicators.note: spanning means the bishop's letters stretch across either side of the years

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
an age is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: A long-serving bishop turns furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A rager is someone who rages, a furious or angry person.

clue.text: Wicked king beat voluntary soldiers and left country briefly

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: briefly means the name of the country is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the USA is a country

explanation.surface: An evil monarch thrashed volunteers and quickly fled the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Tantalus was a king punished in Hades for his crimes, condemned to reach forever for food and water.

clue.text: Nasty b-bit of meat cast into pit

indicators.note: cast into means the meat is dropped inside the pit's letters

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
a rib is a cut of meat, and the stammered b-bit repeats its first letter as R-RIB

explanation.surface: A stammering cook flings a scrap of meat into a pit, which is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'b-bit' tells us to stutter the meat word too, doubling the R of RIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrible means very unpleasant or nasty, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Strong fellow, a joke at first

indicators.note: at first tells us the joke goes in front of the fellow

parts.note: a pun is a joke based on wordplay
a gent, short for gentleman, is a fellow

explanation.surface: A tough man opens with a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent smell or taste is a strong, sharp one, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Fellow with no money at all needing a change of direction

indicators.note: a change of direction swaps one compass-free direction, right, for the other, left

parts.note: broke means having no money whatsoever

explanation.surface: A penniless man needs to turn his life around.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloke is informal British slang for a man or fellow.

clue.text: A hope that may go up in smoke?

definitions.text: A hope that may go up in smoke?

parts.words: A hope that may go up in smoke?
parts.note: a fanciful hope, read literally as a dream rising from a smoker's bowl, evoking opium visions

explanation.surface: A wish that could easily vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantastic, unrealistic hope is named after the visions of opium smokers.

clue.text: Where to drink at home — end of garden

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word garden

explanation.surface: Have a drink at home at the bottom of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, a place where people go to drink.

clue.text: A drug, fixed amount? It may provide fizz

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A medicine in a set dose turns out to be bubbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeration means charging a liquid with gas, which is what produces bubbles in a drink.

clue.text: A lot of lies from children meeting teacher initially?

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word teacher

parts.note: issue means offspring or children, especially in legal language

explanation.surface: Kids tell a pack of fibs when they meet the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a tissue of lies' means a web of untruths, which is why the word stands for a lot of lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue in the idiom 'a tissue of lies' means an interwoven mass or web of falsehoods.

clue.text: I am getting on to motorway grid to move to new territory

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
MI stands for the M1, Britain's first motorway, with the digit read as a letter I
a grate is a metal grid over a fireplace or drain

explanation.surface: Someone joins the motorway at a grid to travel somewhere new.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: To immigrate is to come and settle in a new country, so moving into fresh territory.

clue.text: Low-minded policy that limits play at Wimbledon

parts.note: base means mean or low-minded
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited rule restricts how tennis is played at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis tournament; the baseline is the back line of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: The baseline marks the back boundary of a tennis court, beyond which the ball is out.

clue.text: Cook fish early on

definitions.meaning: to cook something in hot fat in a pan
the young of fish, just hatched, are called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: Fry is both a verb for cooking in fat and the word for very young fish.

clue.text: Coming to and feeling the pain come back?

parts.note: the prefix re- means back or again, so the pain returns
aching means feeling pain

explanation.surface: Someone regains consciousness and feels the pain return.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching means arriving at, so it is a synonym for coming to a place.

clue.text: The fellow touching maiden where the skirt ends

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male, the fellow
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A man is touching a girl at the bottom of her skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hem is the folded, stitched edge of a garment, so the bottom of a skirt.

clue.text: Artist in restaurant gets less than a whole bottle of wine?

definitions.text: less than a whole bottle of wine?

indicators.note: in tells us the artist sits inside the word for an eatery

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
RA, Royal Academician, is a common crossword term for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter dining out receives only part of a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass jug used to serve house wine, often holding less than a full bottle.

clue.text: Copy making up bulk of paper

indicators.note: the bulk of means the main body, here the letters of the word paper without its ends

explanation.surface: A copy forms most of the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate or copy them.

clue.text: Evil drink may lead to good chanting

parts.note: sin is evil or wrongdoing
gin is a drink, a spirit

explanation.surface: Wicked boozing may lead to some pleasant chanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing is making music with the voice, close in sense to chanting.

clue.text: Norm accompanies one Welsh girl in a foreign capital

parts.note: par is the norm or standard level
I is the Roman numeral for one
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A conventional chap joins a young Welsh woman abroad in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Parisian, as an adjective, describes something found in or belonging to Paris, the French capital.

clue.text: A depression very briefly set in? It suggests Christmas is coming!

indicators.note: set in means the short form of very is placed inside the dent

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood setting in hints that Christmas is near.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the season of four weeks leading up to Christmas, marking its approach.

clue.text: Requirement to keep dry and secure in fishing boat?

indicators.note: to keep means the requirement holds the dry letters inside it

parts.note: a need is a requirement
TT, teetotal, means dry or not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Something is needed to keep fish dry and safe in a trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: Netted means caught in a net, the way a catch is secured on a fishing boat.

clue.text: Mused, being sent back

definitions.meaning: pondered or thought deeply about something
bounced back, as light from a mirror

explanation.definitionFit: Reflected means both thought carefully and thrown back, like light or sound.

clue.text: Intelligible and not completely ridiculous on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means the chosen letters are mirrored, read backwards
not completely means only part of the word ridiculous is used, an inner run of letters

explanation.surface: A remark turns out to be clear and not entirely absurd once you think it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' takes DICUL from inside ridiculous; 'on reflection' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear and easy to understand, so a synonym for intelligible.

clue.text: Man of words I understand mostly, given time

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used without its last letter

parts.note: roger is radio slang for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A wordsmith says he mostly gets it, given time.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous thesaurus, so he was a man devoted to words.

clue.text: Is copper tucking into portion that can be eaten?

indicators.note: tucking into means the other letters are slipped inside the portion

parts.note: a bit is a portion or piece
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman asks whether he may dig into his share of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A biscuit is a small baked snack, something made to be eaten.

clue.text: Example set by weird ancients

indicators.note: weird suggests something strange or out of order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Some odd old people set a precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single example or case of something.

clue.text: Salt that ruins dosage

indicators.note: ruins means wrecks, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Salt in the wrong amount spoils the dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is not seasoning: an old salt is an experienced sailor. 'ruins' rearranges DOSAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both salt and sea dog are informal words for an experienced old sailor.
